simple.meaning: עׇרְלָה (ʻorlâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “the prepuce.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 17:11. The surrounding context includes birth, family, family line, covenant.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עׇרְלָה (H6190) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

timeline.evidenceText: You shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin. It will be a token of the covenant between me and you.
The uncircumcised male who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin, that soul shall be cut off from his people. He has broken my covenant.”

Abraham took Ishmael his son, all who were born in his house, and all who were bought with his money: every male among the men of Abraham’s house, and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin in the same day, as God had said to him.
Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
Ishmael, his son, was thirteen years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
and said to them, “We can’t do this thing, to give our sister to one who is uncircumcised; for that is a reproach to us.
Then Zipporah took a flint, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it at his feet; and she said, “Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me.”
In the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.

“ ‘When you come into the land, and have planted all kinds of trees for food, then you shall count their fruit as forbidden.† literally, “uncircumcised” For three years it shall be forbidden to you. It shall not be eaten.
Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiff-necked.
Joshua made himself flint knives, and circumcised the sons of Israel at the hill of the foreskins.

Saul said, “Tell David, ‘The king desires no dowry except one hundred foreskins of the Philistines, to be avenged of the king’s enemies.’ ” Now Saul thought he would make David fall by the hand of the Philistines.

David arose and went, he and his men, and killed two hundred men of the Philistines. Then David brought their foreskins, and they gave them in full number to the king, that he might be the king’s son-in-law. Then Saul gave him Michal his daughter as wife.
David sent messengers to Ishbosheth, Saul’s son, saying, “Deliver me my wife Michal, whom I was given to marry for one hundred foreskins of the Philistines.”

Circumcise yourselves to Yahweh, and take away the foreskins of your heart, you men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem; lest my wrath go out like fire, and burn so that no one can quench it, because of the evil of your doings.
But let him who glories glory in this,

definitions.full: H6190. orlah עָרְלָה 16 noun feminine foreskin ; — ׳ע Gen 34:14 ; Jer 9:24 ; construct עָרְלַת Exod 4:25 ; Deut 10:16 , etc.; plural הָעֲרָלוֺת (not ׳ֳ ) Josh 5:3 (Kö ii. 1, 158 ); construct עָרְלוֺת Jer 4:4 2 t.; עָרְלֹתֵיהֶם 1Sam 18:27 ; — foreskin 18:25 , 27 ; 2Sam 3:14 , compare הָעֲרָלוֺם נִּבְעַת Josh 5:3 hill of the foreskins , near Gilgal; of circumcision, ע ׳כרת Exod 4:25 (J), ע ׳בְּשַׂר Gen 17:11 5 t. P (see II. מוּל ), ע ׳לוֺ אֲשֶׁר אִישׁ 34:14 (P), i.e. one uncircumcised; compare Jer 9:24 ; figurative of fruit trees, עָרְלָתוֺ Lev 19:23 (P; see [ עָרַל ]; figurative of heart, ׳ע לבב Deut 10:16 ; Jer 4:4 .
